Key achievements of this project include: • Development of ECCOsorb-T1, a high capacity, stable DAC sorbent that uses mild regeneration temperature (70°C) and can achieve >5 wt% CO capture in less than 30 minutes 2 • Production of 50 kg of sorbent, including in-house quality assurance testing, for subsequent manufacturing of coated filter • Validation that the structured sorbent filter manufacturing can be conducted using the existing industrial filter manufacturing infrastructure. • Design and fabrication of 1 kg CO /day bench-scale DAC unit to house and test the structured 2 sorbent filters • Estimated CO capture cost reduction from $349/tCO to $241/tCO 2 2 2 • Identification of cost reduction pathway to reach $165/tCO . 2 • Cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment confirming carbon negative performance with renewable electricity sources Final Technical Report – Unlimited Rights Data 28 Susteon Inc. DE-FE0032254 The project team identified key challenges to address in continuation of commercially relevant technology development. Further collaboration with a filter manufacturer is necessary to mitigate the negative impacts of the sorbent adhesive and optimize the sorbent layering process with the aim of improving structured sorbent performance. A deeper understanding of short- and long-term manufacturing costs will also be required. Beyond upgrades to the structured sorbent filter manufacturing, the TEA suggests continued improvements to the sorbent composition to improve CO working capacity and kinetics can further reduce 2 the cost of capture to boost the commercial viability of this technology.
